Real return = nominal return − CPI inflation over the same window.
Reading nominal vs real returns
A nominal return measures dollars; a real return measures purchasing power.
Gold's job as an inflation hedge is judged in
real
terms — if the
CPI rises 80% over a period and gold rises 90%, the real return is only
about
+5.5%
, not 90%.
Historical bottom-line: across 25-year windows, gold has consistently delivered
positive
real
returns. Over shorter windows (1-3 years) it can lose to
inflation in nominal-strong USD periods. This is why gold is treated as a
long-term store of value, not a short-term inflation play.
